content_units: Starting Point and Best-Fit Analyst Path
- You already have 3 strong assets:   SaaS domain knowledge  ,   customer/process intuition  , and   strong Excel  .
- With   8 hours/week for 24 weeks  , you have roughly   190-200 hours   to make a credible transition without going back to school full-time.

- The smartest path is not only “Junior Data Analyst.” Prioritize adjacent roles that value your background:   Support Operations Analyst, Customer Experience Analyst, Reporting Analyst, Product Operations Analyst, Junior Data Analyst  .
- Your   CAD 65,000-75,000   target is most realistic through those adjacent analyst roles first, then pure analyst titles once your portfolio is live.
24-Week Transition Roadmap
Phase   Goal   Key Tasks   Deliverable

Weeks 1-4   Set your analyst foundation   Pick target titles; audit any reporting/metrics work from support; refresh advanced Excel; practice SQL 3 times/week; create GitHub and update LinkedIn headline   Analyst-focused LinkedIn; first resume draft; 20 solved SQL exercises

Weeks 5-8   Get solid in analyst SQL   Learn joins, CASE, GROUP BY, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, date logic; define business KPIs like ticket volume, SLA, CSAT, backlog   SQL mini-case with clean queries and short insights write-up

Weeks 9-12   Learn BI and dashboarding   Choose   Power BI   first; learn Power Query, data modeling basics, simple DAX; build a dashboard from support-style data   Portfolio Project 1 published with screenshots and README

Weeks 13-16   Add light Python and deeper analysis   Learn Python basics: pandas, CSV/Excel cleaning, simple charts; keep SQL strong; build a second project with business recommendations   Portfolio Project 2 on GitHub with notebook and summary

Weeks 17-20   Package yourself for the market   Rewrite resume bullets around analysis and operations impact; create project pages; start networking with Toronto/Canada analyst professionals; do mock interviews   Final resume; polished LinkedIn; 30-company target list

Weeks 21-24   Run a focused job-search sprint   Apply to 8-12 targeted roles/week; send 5 networking messages/week; practice SQL + dashboard walkthroughs + STAR stories; refine based on interviews   50-70 quality applications; 8-12 screening conversations; interview-ready portfolio
-   Weekly split:   Weeks 1-8 = 6h skills + 2h SQL practice; Weeks 9-16 = 4h skills + 3h projects + 1h networking; Weeks 17-24 = 3h skills + 2h portfolio + 3h job search.
Skills to Build in Priority Order
1.   SQL for analysis
- Highest priority and most common screening skill.
- Target: joins, aggregation, CTEs, window functions, date handling, KPI calculations.
- Finish line: you can answer business questions from raw tables without help.
2.   Power BI
- Best next tool because it turns your work into something hiring managers can see fast.
- Target: Power Query, relationships, calculated columns/measures, filters, dashboard design.
- Finish line: 2 shareable dashboards with clear business takeaways.
3.   Analyst-style Excel
- You already have an edge here; convert it into proof of analyst thinking.
- Target: Power Query, PivotTables, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, basic scenario analysis, charting.
- Finish line: one polished Excel analysis you would be comfortable showing in an interview.
4.   Business metrics and storytelling
- This is where your support background becomes valuable.
- Learn: SLA, first response time, resolution time, CSAT, churn signals, cohort thinking, trend analysis.
- Finish line: every project ends with “what matters, why it matters, what action to take.”
5.   Python basics
- Important, but not blocker number one for your first analyst job.
- Target: pandas, reading CSV/Excel, cleaning data, grouping, merging, simple plots.
- Finish line: one notebook that cleans data and produces insights.
6.   GitHub and presentation
- Many career switchers lose interviews here.
- Target: simple repos, strong README, screenshots, business summary, clean file names.
- Finish line: each project is understandable in under 2 minutes.
7.   Light statistics
- Learn only what helps interviews and project interpretation.
- Focus: averages vs medians, percent change, correlation vs causation, distributions, confidence basics.
- Skip deep theory for now.
-   Do not prioritize yet:   machine learning, advanced Python, long bootcamps, heavy math, or a full diploma before applying.
Portfolio Projects That Match Your Background
Option 1: Support KPI Dashboard   Analyze ticket volume, SLA, backlog, CSAT, and resolution trends   Best bridge from SaaS support to analytics
- Tools: SQL + Power BI + Excel
- Show: trend lines, issue categories, peak periods, agent/team comparisons, 3 recommendations
- Why it works: it proves you can turn familiar operations data into decisions
Action: [Button: Find data] < >
Option 2: SaaS Churn and Retention Analysis   Explore support activity, product usage, and renewal/churn patterns   Strongest project for higher-paying adjacent analyst roles
- Tools: SQL + Excel or Python + Power BI
- Show: churn-risk segments, cohort retention, feature/support behavior by account type
- Why it works: it connects support knowledge to revenue impact
Action: [Button: Data playground] < >
Option 3: Toronto Service Request Trend Analysis   Use local public data to build a city-level dashboard and insight brief   Good proof of real-world data cleaning and communication
- Tools: Excel + SQL + Power BI
- Show: request volume by neighborhood/category/season, turnaround patterns, operational bottlenecks
- Why it works: it adds a non-support project and shows broader analyst ability
Action: [Button: Toronto data] < >
- For each project, publish:
- a   1-paragraph business problem
-   clean screenshots
-   3-5 key findings
-   2-3 recommendations
- a short   README
- That is more valuable than building 8 unfinished projects.
Resume Repositioning for Analyst Roles
Use this headline
-   Customer Support Analyst transitioning to Data Analyst   Excel, SQL, Power BI   SaaS Operations Insights
Use this summary

- Data-minded SaaS support professional with 3 years of experience translating customer issues into operational insights. Strong in Excel, building SQL skills, and creating clear KPI reporting. Seeking Toronto or remote Canada roles in junior data analysis, support operations, or reporting where customer and product context can improve business decisions.
Rewrite your experience around analysis, not only service
- “Handled customer tickets” →   Analyzed recurring issue patterns and escalation drivers across support cases to identify product and process pain points.
- “Met response targets” →   Tracked and improved support KPIs such as response time, resolution time, backlog, and SLA adherence.
- “Worked with product/engineering” →   Partnered cross-functionally to convert customer issue trends into actionable feedback for product and operations teams.
- “Built spreadsheets/reports” →   Used Excel reporting to summarize trends, monitor team performance, and support operational decision-making.
Add a skills block that feels job-relevant
- SQL, Excel, Power Query, PivotTables, Power BI, dashboarding, data cleaning, KPI reporting, stakeholder communication, SaaS support operations
What to downplay
- Long lists of ticketing tools
- Generic customer service soft skills
- “Learning Python” as a headline skill before you can demonstrate it
Job Search System for Toronto and Remote Canada
1) Target these job titles first
- Support Operations Analyst
- Customer Experience Analyst
- Reporting Analyst
- Operations Analyst
- Product Operations Analyst
- Junior Data Analyst
- Business Analyst roles with heavy reporting/KPI work
2) Use a tiered application strategy
-   Tier 1:   SaaS companies where support analytics is a clear need
-   Tier 2:   Fintech, healthtech, e-commerce, marketplaces, logistics
-   Tier 3:   Broader junior analyst roles where SQL + BI + business context matter more than advanced Python
3) Apply with volume, but only after project 1 is live
- Start serious applications around   Week 17
- Target   8-12 tailored applications/week
- Aim for   50-70 quality applications   over the final 2 months, not 200 generic ones
4) Network in a way that actually works
- Send   5 short messages/week   to analysts, support ops leads, and BI/reporting managers in Toronto or remote Canadian companies
- Message format:
- 1 line on shared context
- 1 line on your pivot
- 1 specific question about the role/team
- Better than asking directly for a referral on first contact
5) Prepare for the interviews you will actually get
- SQL screening: practice 2-3 query problems per week
- Portfolio walkthrough: explain the business question, dataset, method, insight, recommendation
- STAR stories: prepare 4 stories on process improvement, trend spotting, stakeholder communication, and customer pain-point analysis
6) Make your background feel like an advantage
- Your narrative should be:
“I already understand operational data, customer behavior, recurring issues, and business impact. I’m adding the technical stack to analyze that more formally.”
- That is stronger than:
“I’m leaving support and starting over.”
7) Keep this realistic
- The fastest route to your target pay is likely   adjacent analytics roles   first, not only generic junior data analyst postings.
- Once you have 6-12 months in an analyst title, your next move becomes much easier.
